segments.text: A family dispute rarely starts in court. It starts with a missing document, an unclear nominee, or two people remembering the same property differently.
R B I research finds about 84 percent of Indian household wealth sits in property and other physical assets.
C P R reports land and property make up roughly 66 percent of civil cases in the cited research.
NITI Aayog cites almost 20 years for a land-acquisition dispute to reach resolution.
N J D G currently shows over 5.18 crore pending district and taluka cases. 1.13 crore of them civil.
On Record starts before the dispute, while Mihir Sharma is alive.
He records what exists: the home, financial assets, documents, nominee status, and his wishes.
Everything starts private.
He then chooses what his spouse Ananya can see. Existence-only, so she knows a record exists without seeing sensitive details.
This is Ananya's view. Not Mihir's account. A separate, read-only perspective showing only what he approved.
The same case then moves into a handover. Mihir selects the facts needed later and prepares a simulated read-only file.
The feature I rebuilt is the Consent Fork.
Most systems treat sharing as one irreversible decision. On Record separates three moments.
The owner's private living record.
What each person can see now.
And what may be handed over later.

Every record carries nominee status, because the process is institution-specific. R B I explains a nominee may receive funds as trustee for the legal heirs. So On Record records the nomination, never the ownership.
A visibility downgrade is not instant. It enters a simulated seven-day cooling-off period. Concerns can be raised without edit access. Every material change writes a Consent Log entry.
The recipient receives a separate handover file. Never the owner's account.
On Record does not make a will, decide ownership, or replace a court, bank, or authority.
It helps families reach those processes with fewer missing facts, fewer conflicting memories, and clearer consent.
The goal is simple. Prevent a family record from becoming a family dispute.
